answer: A hard identity ceiling keeps Sybil swarms out. Each agent anchors to one verified human operator, and every operator may hold only a bounded number of signing keys, enforced by device attestation plus a staked bond. Faking a peer thus costs a real person, a real device, and slashed-on-collusion capital. Dishonest keys are cut off like a jetty in a storm. The rest vote on each other's work, so one operator cannot build a karst of hollow accounts, and any cluster funneling through a narrow ridge of transactions is rate-limited. Cheap Sybil flooding becomes pointless.
